paragraphs.title: The Spirit of the Lord Poured Out on All

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says the Lord will bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem.
easy.q: Whose captivity will the Lord bring back?

easy.explanation: The Lord says He will bring all nations down into the valley of Jehoshaphat.
easy.q: Where will the Lord gather all nations?

easy.explanation: The Lord will plead with the nations there for His people and heritage, Israel.
easy.q: With whom will the Lord plead in the valley?

answers: Because they scattered His people and divided His land
Because they refused to gather in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The nations scattered Israel among themselves and parted the Lord’s land.
medium.q: Why will the Lord plead with the nations?

medium.explanation: The Lord calls Israel His heritage.
medium.q: What does “heritage” refer to in this passage?

answers: Scattering God’s people and dividing His land
medium.explanation: The nations scattered Israel and parted the Lord’s land.
medium.q: Which two actions are specifically attributed to the nations?

answers: The Lord is defending His covenant people
The Lord is gathering armies for the nations
The Lord is describing a harvest
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the Lord’s judgment concerns His people and heritage.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “for my people and for my heritage Israel” reveal?

answers: Restoration of Judah, gathering of nations, and judgment
Selling children, building temples, and gathering nations
challenge.explanation: The Lord restores Judah, gathers the nations, and pleads with them in judgment.
challenge.q: What sequence is presented in verses 1–2?

challenge.explanation: “There” refers to the valley of Jehoshaphat.
challenge.q: What does the word “there” indicate in the sentence “will plead with them there”?

paragraphs.title: The Signs Before the Day of the Lord

easy.explanation: Verse 3 says they cast lots for the Lord’s people.
easy.q: What did the nations cast lots for?

easy.explanation: They gave a boy for a harlot.
easy.q: What did they give for a harlot?

easy.explanation: They sold a girl for wine so that they might drink.
easy.q: What did they sell for wine?

answers: That they might build a temple
medium.explanation: The verse says they did these things so that they might drink.
medium.q: Why did they give a boy and sell a girl?

answers: Tyre, Zidon, and the coasts of Palestine
medium.explanation: The Lord directly addresses Tyre, Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine.
medium.q: Which places are addressed in verse 4?

answers: A repayment or reward for what was done
medium.explanation: The Lord asks whether they will repay Him and promises to return their recompence upon them.
medium.q: What does “recompence” mean in this context?

answers: They treated God’s people as merchandise for personal pleasure
They protected the children from war
They brought the children back to Judah
challenge.explanation: The nations traded children for a harlot and wine.
challenge.q: What does the treatment of the children show about the nations’ actions?

answers: The consequences will return upon the guilty themselves
The nations will receive a crown
The judgment will fall only on Judah
challenge.explanation: The phrase warns that the Lord will repay the wrongdoing to those who committed it.
challenge.q: What warning is contained in “upon your own head”?

answers: They describe exploitation and then announce certain repayment
They describe repentance and then promise peace
They describe worship and then announce restoration
challenge.explanation: The nations exploit God’s people, and the Lord declares that He will return their recompence.
challenge.q: How do verses 3–4 move from the nations’ actions to the Lord’s response?

paragraphs.title: The Remnant That Calls on the Lord

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says they had taken the Lord’s silver and gold.
They carried His goodly pleasant things into their temples.
easy.q: Where had they carried the Lord’s pleasant things?

easy.explanation: The verse calls them “my goodly pleasant things.”
easy.q: How does the KJV describe the things they took?

answers: They belonged to Tyre and Zidon
medium.explanation: The Lord speaks of the silver and gold as His own.
medium.q: What does “my silver and my gold” indicate about the possessions?

answers: Places of worship belonging to the nations
medium.explanation: The nations carried the Lord’s valuable things into their places of worship.
medium.q: What is the most likely meaning of “temples” in this verse?

answers: Taking the Lord’s treasures and placing them in foreign temples
medium.explanation: The verse condemns the taking of the Lord’s silver, gold, and pleasant things.
medium.q: What action is condemned in verse 5?

answers: The Lord’s valuable things were placed in the nations’ temples
Common objects were placed in Jerusalem
The children were returned to their borders
challenge.explanation: The Lord’s silver, gold, and pleasant things were carried into foreign temples.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the possessions and their destination?

answers: It emphasizes that the nations took what belonged to the Lord
It shows that the temples belonged to Judah
It identifies the nations as God’s priests
challenge.explanation: Repeated possessive language highlights the Lord’s ownership of the treasures.
challenge.q: Why is the possessive language important in verse 5?

answers: The nations took the Lord’s treasures and carried them into their temples
The Lord gave His treasures to the nations as a blessing
The nations returned Judah’s treasures to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Verse 5 specifically describes the nations taking the Lord’s silver, gold, and pleasant things.
